identity.realm: Fourth, and the ceiling of her species, cleared on the mind ladder and reachable on no other. The body path is closed to a rootmarch outright, because there is no tissue to temper and wood is not muscle and cannot be made to be. The qi ladder stops at the fourth for a structural reason: three sap columns branch but never pair, so there is no channel running between distinct pairs of them for the yin-organ gate to close, and the gate set is cleared on stored sap alone. The mind ladder ends at the same fourth rung as everybody else's below the fifth, but for the opposite reason and with a different residue on it, because the fourth rung is where the Mind path makes its founding claim and hers is the only body in the record that has answered it. She is the only rootmarch entered on any ladder anywhere.

appearance.presentation: A woody column on a root foot, planted at the edge of a bedding ground the Field Registry has never entered on a sheet, distinguishable from every other rootmarch on that slope by a second plate low on her sunward side that no surveyor has recorded. It sits two paces off her collar, it never sets, and it draws while the column above it is drawing nothing. A settlement marks her approach by the plate, which moves before she does.
appearance.age: Ninety-one growing seasons, rooted since the fourth. The second plate is sixty-eight seasons old, which makes it the oldest thing on that slope anybody can name a start for.
appearance.build: Dense and columnar, wider at the fruiting shoulder than at the collar, three sap columns running as ridges under the bark and not one of them paired. The second plate has widened her footprint by about a third without putting any mass above the collar line, so all of her weight still sits low and the shape above the plate reads narrower than it did when she was planted.
appearance.complexion: Bark silvered on the sunward flank and sap-dark down at the plate line, the flanks flushing a translucent yellow-green in good light and going flat olive in shade. The plate is a different colour from the column it came out of: redder, wetter, and it flushes a season behind her, which is the only thing about her that anybody on that slope has ever taken seriously.
appearance.hair: None. A short dry crest of old collar-plate worked into the wood year on year by whatever last cut the plate, and a fringe of new copper growth at the crown that stands up before anything else on her does.
appearance.eyes: Two slow light-organs set wide and low on the flanks, opening one at a time, neither of them ever quite shut. The plate has none of its own, which means it cannot notice anything and takes its entire account of a season from the column above it.
appearance.palette: Dust ochre, silver-grey bark, sap green held well below the green of living wood, one band of copper at the crown, and a wet red on the plate that appears nowhere else on her.
appearance.attire: A bark-cloth wrap over the fruiting shoulder and a band of river stone laid across the second plate and tied at nothing, because the plate is what is holding her down and the band is the only thing anybody has ever asked her to wear. Nothing else has ever been fitted to her.
appearance.marks: A seasonal cut ring at the root plate, renewed every year, and a second and much older ring around the plate, cut once and never renewed, because renewing it would kill it. There is no name cut on her anywhere, and the Registry's entry reads as a bed and a season and has never once contained a second object.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried, and impossible to approach from above. The whole of her bearing is the interval between a thing happening over her head and her beginning to answer it, and the interval is now visibly different on her two sides: the column answers at the speed of a light sense and the plate answers a season later, so she appears to make up her mind twice about the same thing.

canon.role_in_story: Every Mind tradition in the setting rests on one claim: that the self being cultivated can be separated from the one doing the cultivating. The fourth rung is where that claim is made, and at that band there is no spatial imprint, so the claim is asserted rather than shown and nobody in the record has ever shown it. Hesper Ullmarch has been at that rung for sixty-eight seasons and has answered it, by accident and then by maintenance, with a second root plate she put down herself and has kept alive ever since. The plate is not a fruit and it does not set. It draws out of the same soil as her column, at its own times, running about a season behind the column, and for two documented stretches it held a season the column could not hold, which is the entire content of the claim: one thing in her, fed by her, surviving on what she did not send it. She is the only demonstration the setting has, and it is filed as a crop. The Field Registry certifies which bed a lineage came from, and the register for her species is a seed ledger in which the only thing worth certifying is the bed; a plate is not a bed, a law's tier list says where it may apply and a seat says where it is actually installed, and there is no column anywhere in the setting for a second object a body produced and then kept. She is therefore not the evidence for anything. She is the case somebody would have to reopen if the claim were ever to stop being an article of faith, and the cost of reopening it is that the only technique capable of testing it works by dissolving the distinction she has spent sixty-eight seasons holding up.
canon.first_appearance: First entered the record as a correction that could not be made. A surveyor from the Registry set a line along her bed and counted her shoulders by the method used on every rootmarch, and came back with one, having seen two. The second thing he saw was not a shoulder. It was the plate, which sits at a different angle from the column and moves when she does not. He wrote one into the sheet, because a rootmarch carries one fruiting shoulder in its life and he was correct about that, and the sheet has said one at every reweighing ever since. What he did not write, and could not have, is that the object he entered in the wrong column of his own count is the only part of her that anybody is currently cultivating.
canon.lore: A rootmarch is a woody column body on a root foot, with three sap columns and no organ pairs. There is no mouth in the ordinary sense, because intake happens through root plates, which are also the chemoreceptive organ, so everything this body takes in from the world arrives through the one part of it that is underground and cannot be sealed from above by anyone standing over it. Photosynthetic flanks carry the light sense and that sense is slow, so she is slow to react and impossible to surprise from above, because being surprised requires noticing and noticing requires a light organ working. She flowers once in her life. The fruit drops, the seed takes root, and the dangerous part of that is establishment rather than conception, which is why the register for this species is a seed ledger and the only thing worth certifying is which bed a lineage came from. The body path is closed to her outright, because there is no tissue to temper and wood is not muscle. The qi ladder is complete as far as it goes and stops at the fourth, because three unpaired sap columns leave no channel running between distinct pairs for the yin-organ gate to close. The mind path is open, on the recorded ground that a plant lineage has no reason to be hurried, and the fourth rung of it is the rung at which the self being cultivated becomes separable from the one doing the cultivating. Her species is also the setting's standing famine reserve, a body engineered upward out of a mycorrhizal crop because a plant lineage is the only one that can hold a harvest across a famine, and a body that lives on stored sap and cannot be moved once rooted without being injured. Put those two facts together and a question appears that nobody has ever put in writing. A plant is not one self. It puts down secondary roots off its own column, and a secondary root is demonstrably part of the plant, demonstrably not the same object as the column, demonstrably fed by it, and demonstrably able to survive a stretch the column cannot. That is the Mind path's founding claim, arriving in a body that has been doing it for longer than the setting has been recording, without ever being asked to file anything. Hesper put a plate down at twenty-three seasons because a bad year had taken the seedling she was banking on and she wanted something of hers in the ground before the next one. She cut the plate's ring once and never cut it again. Everything since has been one discipline of a single kind: keeping the plate's account of a season separate from the column's, when both are fed by the same soil and neither can be shut off from the other. It has worked because the plate runs behind the column by about a season, which makes the difference between them measurable in ordinary time rather than in argument. It has never once been filed, because what she has is not a law group and not a bed and not a seed. It is a second plate, and there is no seat for it.
history: Was planted at four growing seasons into ground broken for her specifically at the foot of the Spirit Peaks, and entered in the Field Registry as a bed and a season, which is the whole of what a rootmarch entry has ever contained for any of them.

Put a second root plate down at twenty-three seasons, into the same bed, two paces off her collar, after a bad year had taken the one seedling she was relying on and she wanted something of hers in the ground before the next one arrived.

Cut the plate's ring once in the following season and never cut it again, on the reasoning that renewing a cut ring is how a rootmarch survives being moved and how a plate that is not her survives being killed, and she has held that decision for sixty-eight seasons on the strength of one cut.

Cleared the fourth gate on stored sap in her twenty-ninth season, which is the ceiling of her species and the same rung at which the Mind path makes its founding claim, and worked out in the same decade that her species has no fifth and that the claim is therefore the last thing her ladder will ever ask her.

Kept the one-season lag between the plate and the column as the only evidence that the two of them are separable, and twice declined an invitation to have the plate cut and the question closed, which would have been easier for everyone and would have left the setting exactly where it already was.

personality.summary: Not a temperament so much as a long bookkeeping habit that other people have decided is a temperament. She has drawn one conclusion from sixty-eight seasons of maintaining a thing the register has no column for, and she has organised every part of herself around it: that the distinction is real, that it is hers to keep, and that the keeping is the whole of her usefulness. What reads as obstinacy is an audit. What reads as patience is a body that literally cannot hurry. What reads as indifference to the Registry is the only available form of self-respect left to a body the Registry files under ground.
traits: keeps the plate and the column on separate ledgers by season, in her head, for sixty-eight seasons, and has never written either down
answers any question twice, the column first at light-sense speed and the plate a season behind, and has never once pretended the second answer was the first
reads her own flanks for light and shade with a precision no instrument on the Spirit Peaks can match, and applies that precision to nothing else

has never attempted a fifth gate and does not describe the absence as a loss

mannerisms: tips the fruiting shoulder toward whoever is speaking and then, a season later in every observable respect, tips the plate the same way

will not accept water from a hand that has touched the plate that season
renews the root ring every year in front of whoever is watching, and does it the same way every time, which is the only ritual any of them has
motivations: wants the plate kept off the record, which is the same want as keeping it alive, and has never separated the two
wants the lag between the two of her bodies measured by somebody else exactly once, so that the measurement exists whether or not she does
wants the fourth rung reopened as a question rather than settled as an article, and has wanted it since her twenty-ninth season
wants to see the fruit taken and planted and does not want to be told by whom
flaws: cannot be distinguished from her bed by any instrument on the tier, and has turned that from a nuisance into the ground of every protection she has
cannot say a number out loud without a second body agreeing to it, so the one figure she is competent to hold is the one figure she is least able to act on
has maintained a single cut for sixty-eight seasons on reasoning rather than evidence, and has twice been wrong about that in the same direction
reads her own decline as a season rather than as a fault, exactly as every rootmarch does, and has no way to tell the difference
has never once asked anybody for anything, and can no longer reconstruct what she would have asked for
personality.voice: There is no mouth in the ordinary sense, because intake happens through root plates, so the body other people address as a speaker has no apparatus for it. What she has instead is a slow flush across the photosynthetic flank that runs toward whoever is nearest when she has understood something and stays flat when she has not, and a red flush on the plate a season behind it that everybody on that slope reads without ever once calling either of them a language. She is patient with questions at the exact limit of what a light sense can resolve in one season, and she names things by what they will have become rather than by what they are, which makes her very hard to argue with and very easy to misread.
taboos: will not have the plate entered on a sheet, a bed map, a seed ledger or a survey
will not be lifted while rooting, and will refuse a cart as calmly as a person
will not accept a name cut into her bark, on the ground that a name on a commons is a claim and she is not claiming anything
will not attempt a fifth gate, and treats the question as settled rather than pending
will not have her ground turned while she is standing on it, whoever asks and for whatever reason

relationships.kind: the body she is and the ladder that stops at her

Everything that makes her species durable and cheap to keep is also what makes it impossible to select, aim at or measure, and she has spent ninety-one seasons as the standing example of that trade.

relationships.kind: the rung that made her species the answer to its own founding claim
relationships.note: The fourth rung is where the self being cultivated becomes separable from the one doing the cultivating, and at that band no spatial imprint exists, so the claim is asserted rather than shown. She is at that rung, and she has a thing in her body that has already answered it, and the band has no instrument capable of registering the answer.

relationships.kind: the only test of her claim and the one thing she cannot survive
relationships.note: It floods a mind's own recall until a real memory and a planted one stop being distinguishable, and it is entirely water, so fire burns it out. It is the single technique in the codex that would settle her whole claim, and it works by destroying exactly the distinction her claim rests on, which is why a rootmarch who has maintained one for sixty-eight seasons cannot be the one to run it.

relationships.kind: the count that produced her ceiling and has no place for her plate
relationships.note: Counting laws against seats and getting an answer that did not change is what settled what a body can be, and it is the reason her qi ladder stops where it does. It is also the reason her demonstration has never been entered: a law's tier list says where it may apply and a seat says where it is installed, and a second root plate is neither, so the register had nothing to write against.

relationships.kind: the obvious answer that does not fit, and she is it
relationships.note: Strata under the plains carry tool marks implying a hand on a frame that seats three law groups and none of them moves distance, so no hand could have worked them. This is the only body in the setting that could have made marks in strata without moving anything at all, so her lineage is the obvious answer, and it does not fit, because a rootmarch has no hand and could not have cut what was found. She is standing on the wrong side of her own usefulness.

relationships.kind: the practice her species is the limiting case of
relationships.note: A house marks its own threshold and renews the mark when the frame beneath it changes, and admits the mark may hold while the frame does not. Her species' threshold is rooting depth, renewed every season whether or not anything else changed, so she renews a mark that was never at risk, and the mark is the only record of her that has ever existed.

reference_stats.summary: The only body in the setting that is its own control, and the only demonstration in the record of a thing the Mind path has asserted for as long as it has existed. Both facts are the same fact: a second plate, fed from her own bed, running about a season behind her, kept alive by one cut she decided to make at twenty-three and has never repeated. She is also, and for the same reason, the hardest body on the Spirit Peaks to point at, because her qi is held in the sap column and reads as a spread rather than a point.
strengths: holds the season on a bed nobody has improved in ninety seasons, which no body with tissue to maintain can do on ground this old
draws soil qi more efficiently than anything else in the record and cannot demonstrate it to anybody, because the demonstration needs an instrument that can find her
keeps two accounts of every season apart for sixty-eight seasons without an error she has ever been able to detect
answers overhead change before anything else on the ground does, which has made her unapproachable from above and effectively impossible to startle
can outlast a bad year sealed in a dark field, which makes her the setting's famine reserve and a hostage in exactly equal measure
weaknesses: cannot travel once rooted and is injured rather than slowed by being moved, so every option that begins with leaving is closed to her
reads as a spread rather than a point, so no targeting or dosing practice on the tier can isolate her, including where isolation would help her
has no fifth gate to aim at and no successor to hand anything to, because her species flowers once and the seed has to be planted by somebody else
goes still for a whole season at the turn of the weather and is functionally furniture for the duration, with no way to signal that it has started
cannot be rescued either, because a rescue has to locate her first, and that failure looks identical from outside to her being neglected
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to hit her. Her qi is a spread and there is no centre to aim at, so anything sent at the body passes through the space she occupies without meeting anything. The practical consequence is worse than being hard to hit: she cannot be recovered either, because recovery has to find her first. Pressure the bed instead of the frame. Shading the flanks, cutting the plate ring that holds the bed together, or letting the sap run down past a point she cannot reach ends it faster than anything sent at the body. Do not cut the plate to end her faster: that is the one action on this body that also destroys the only demonstration the setting has, and it will look identical to the others afterwards.
notes: Model the plate as a control group that has been running for sixty-eight seasons without a protocol, and treat her as the instrument rather than the subject.
The species closes the body path only. Qi and mind are both open; she is on mind and at her species' ceiling.
Do not give her a gate to attempt above the fourth. The fourth is the end of her ladder for a structural reason, and it is also the last claim her ladder will ever make.
The only technique that could test her demonstration is the one that dissolves the distinction the demonstration rests on, so the dilemma is structural rather than a choice she is avoiding.

identity.realm: Ninth of eleven, and he has said out loud why he stopped there. Every path is open to his species and he is on the mind one, which is the path a crossing is least expected to take, because the crossing widened his range and left his ceiling exactly where the salt parent had put it: the brine sac is smaller in a brinecaller but it is still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split and the eleventh is capped by structure rather than by effort. He is at the ninth, which is the last rung on which the claim the Mind path rests on can be examined and the first on which his own recall stops being evidence for it. Three people have been told the reason and that is the only instance in the setting of anybody stating a floor that is not a shortage of money.

appearance.presentation: A saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus, standing on a stone mole at the mouth of a delta where the brack line runs twice a day and moves the ground under him by about a hundred paces each time. He is the only body on that shore that can stand on either side of the line and read both, and he is the only person anybody there has ever asked to testify to which side he was standing on.
appearance.age: Sixty-four, born on the pan side and raised on the watered side, which is a pairing the petition that governs him has no word for. He has kept both birth records for as long as either has existed and has never been asked which one he will hand over.
appearance.build: Saltfolk spare and tidecaller long, with the rib cage of a body that has to work in moving water and almost no muscle anywhere above it. The shallower sac reads as a smoothing along the spine rather than as a feature, and the dermal intake that lets him drink from either chemistry is a thickening at the forearms and throat that people mistake for a disease.
appearance.complexion: Salt-pale and waxy across the shoulders, undamaged by either water because his body carries two chemistries and reads neither of them as hostile. A standing tide line at each ankle from a life spent on a mole the delta rewrites twice a day, and a habit of going faintly grey-green within an hour of eating anything at all.
appearance.hair: Wet dark and pushed flat, dried stiff with salt at the ends and cut short enough that it never holds the shape of a hat, which is a practical choice on a shore where a hat is a thing you lose at sea.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and slightly rimmed, the best chemical sense in the record, so his eyes fix on a thing the way a dog fixes on a scent rather than the way a person looks. He can tell which chemistry a cup of water holds at a glance and cannot reliably tell you which tide an hour happened in, which is the whole of his difficulty and it is not a small one.
appearance.palette: Salt white and wet slate grey, a green-grey cast wherever his skin is exposed to air for long, counting-house black at the collar and cuffs, and one worn ochre on a leather strap he has replaced twice and will replace again.
appearance.attire: Counting-house grey over saltfolk oilskin, heavy at the shoulder and cut away at the throat so the intake thickening is visible, which the shirt was altered for by a tailor who asked no questions and was paid for the alteration as though it were a uniform rule. Wading boots on a mole, never removed, never resoled.
appearance.marks: A salt-bloom scar across both forearms from a sluice that closed on him, and two ink marks on the inside of his left wrist in a counting house's hand: four short strokes for the four readings he takes of anything, and a longer fifth that means the fifth was a copy.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried and permanently slightly braced, as though the ground under him is scheduled to move and he is respecting the schedule. He turns his head at the turn of the tide whether or not he is looking at anything, which people read as a tic and which is the most reliable thing about him.

canon.role_in_story: On a coast whose temporal law was never written the clock drifts, so no date is the same twice and a schedule has to be published against two tides a day instead of a calendar, and every settlement on that shore speaks in high, low and turning because nothing else there is repeatable. Mereth Kolm is the only body in the record that can hold both of those chemistries at once, which makes him the only person on that shore whose own recall is addressed twice a day with no way to tell which address he is remembering from. That is not a complaint about the calendar. It is the fact that makes the Mind path's founding claim untestable on him: the claim is that the self being cultivated is separable from the one doing the cultivating, and he cannot establish which of his two readings of an afternoon belongs to the one being cultured. His answer is a forgery. He takes an impression, splits it, sends half of it back down the same path, and keeps the half that returns as a marker, because a copy that comes back is provably a copy and therefore identifies the other one as the original. He forges his own recall four times a day so that he can tell which half he is living in, and the forge is the only technique in the codex that returns what it splits. Nobody has asked him why he stopped at the ninth and he has told three people anyway.
canon.first_appearance: First entered the record as a witness who gave two accounts and then corrected the first one in front of the person it was about. The counting house was settling which side of a crossing he had been standing on, and he gave his answer, and then asked for the whole question back so that he could answer it again deliberately, and the second answer came back with a slight difference in it that he had not been able to produce on purpose the first time. He explained the difference by saying the question was asked at high water, and nobody on the floor checked, because he was the only man there who could answer it at all.
canon.lore: A brinecaller is the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones. It exists because both parents are trapped by their own element, one unable to leave the pan and one unable to leave the water, and a crossing is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, which is why the crossing spread along trade routes rather than across open ground. He is a saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus: dermal intake, a wider electrolyte tolerance, and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. His chemical sense is the best in the record by a wide margin, and it is always being lied to by one of the two chemistries it reads. Every path is open to his species and range is not power: the crossing moved his ceiling not at all, because the sac is still dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel is still split, so the eleventh is capped by structure and the mind path is open and good, being the least salted water-adapted body in the record, which is the point of him. The shore he lives on has never had temporal law written in it, so the clock drifts and a schedule is published against two tides a day instead of a calendar, and the civic vocabulary there is high, low and turning because nothing else is repeatable. So his body, which cannot choose one chemistry and does not have to, also cannot choose one clock, and every impression he takes in is therefore addressable twice: once by the tide he is standing in and once by the tide that will follow it. The mind path at his ninth rung asks him to say which of the two he is. He has spent twenty-six years answering by making the question answerable. The technique that returns what it splits is the only one in the codex built for exactly this, so he marks every impression by sending half of it back down its own path and keeping the returning half as the tag. What survives that is a memory with a counterfeit stapled to it, and the counterfeit is what tells him which side of the afternoon he is on. It works. It also means that the one thing his tradition asks him to demonstrate, that the self being cultivated is separable from the one cultivating it, is the one thing he has arranged never to test, because the test requires a clean original and he has spent twenty-six years making sure he never has one.
history: Was born on the pan side of the delta and moved to the watered side at nine months, which is the ordinary crossing pattern and the reason his household survey stopped being either thing four generations back.

Started working the crossing schedule at twenty, marking each reading on his wrist with four short strokes, which is the counting house's method and not his and which he kept after they stopped paying for the marks.

Began the forgery at thirty-eight, after a season in which he could not say which of two afternoons a toll had been paid on, and which cost a carrier a year's margin and cost him the only credential he has ever held.
Stopped climbing at the ninth at forty-six and gave the reason to three people in one winter, unasked each time, and has said nothing further about it since.

Has returned his own copy of the published window for twenty-six seasons, in a hand that is his own and is not, and has been asked twice by the underwriters to stop because a schedule that corrects itself reads as an error to anybody holding the sheet.

personality.summary: Not a personality so much as a method that has worn a person's shape. He has taken one impossibility, the double address of everything he perceives, and answered it with a single technique applied four times a day for twenty-six years, and everything else about him has been arranged around that arrangement holding. What reads as fussiness is tag discipline. What reads as evasiveness is a man who has learned that the unrepeated answer is the expensive one. What reads as coldness is the amount of attention he spends on not being fooled by himself.

personality.voice: Low, unhurried and slightly over-formal, a counting house's cadence in a man who was never admitted to the counting house. He begins with the state of the water and goes on to the question, and he has trained himself to do that so consistently that listeners start leaving out the first part and are then surprised when a claim he makes turns out to have a condition attached. He uses words for the shore rather than for time, which makes him very hard to follow from inland and extremely easy to follow at the mole. He is generous with his method and has never once been generous with a conclusion.
taboos: will not state a date, a year or an hour, and will answer in the shore's vocabulary rather than the counting house's
will not surrender either of his birth records, and will not discuss which of the two he regards as the true one

relationships.kind: the body that reads both chemistries and therefore both clocks
relationships.note: A saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's chest seat, perfectly legible and structurally neither parent. The sac is still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel is still split and the eleventh is capped exactly where the salt parent had it. The crossing widened his range without raising his ceiling, and range is not power.

relationships.kind: the table that gives his recall two addresses
relationships.note: Timekeeping for a coast whose temporal law was never written: the clock drifts, no date is the same twice, and a schedule has to be published against two tides a day instead of a calendar. It is the reason nothing he remembers has one address, and it is a fact about the frame rather than about him, which is why no amount of practice removes it.

relationships.kind: the claim he cannot put to the one body that would settle it
relationships.note: The self being cultivated becomes separable from the one doing the cultivating, and at that band no spatial imprint exists, so the claim is asserted rather than shown. He has reached the rung below it and stopped there on purpose, because a clean original impression is exactly what twenty-six seasons of forgery have made sure he has never once been in a position to supply.

relationships.kind: the technique his whole method is made of
relationships.note: It splits an incoming impression and sends half of it back down the same path, and it is a dark reflection, weakest against light and best against its own kind. Used four times a day on himself it gives him the one thing no calendar on that shore can give: a demonstrable counterfeit, and therefore an identifiable original.

relationships.kind: the question his body is the obvious answer to
relationships.note: One tear has stood open long enough to be named, both sides write the same law group at the same value, and no tide has ever crossed it. A body metabolising both chemistries is the obvious courier for exactly that crossing, which is why the question has a commercial stake nobody has been able to price, and which is why the underwriters keep underwriting a carrier who cannot say when he moved.

relationships.kind: the vocabulary he has instead of a calendar
relationships.note: Nobody on that tideline is inside or outside, only high, low or turning, and the practice exists because an unwritten temporal law means the clock drifts and no date is the same twice. For most people on that shore it is a way of speaking. For him it is the only accurate description of what he perceives, which is why he cannot be the one to explain it.

reference_stats.summary: A body that reads two chemistries at once and therefore reads two clocks at once, and a discipline of one technique applied four times a day to keep the two apart. Everything he is good at comes from the same place as everything he cannot do, and the pair is inseparable: he can tell a stranger's water from their mood at a glance and cannot tell you which half of his own afternoon he is living in. He stopped one rung short on purpose and has told three people so.
strengths: holds the best chemical sense in the record and reads concentration across a room without touching it, which nothing else on either shore can do
returns an impression down its own path and gets a demonstrable counterfeit back, so he can mark his own recall without an instrument, a ledger or a witness
sits out both a dry season on pan brine and a flood on fresh water without a change of body, and is the only population the river's schedule can feed rather than evict
crosses a shoreline with no cut, no cloth credential and no ritual, so no published exclusivity has ever been able to classify him
answers the same question twice on the record, which has made him the only witness on that shore that cannot be caught out on a single telling
weaknesses: cannot name a time in any form an office accepts, so his testimony is routinely filed as an impression rather than as an account
has no native ground anywhere: he needs a shoreline, and a shoreline is the one piece of ground on that coast that both shores have a claim to
depends entirely on a single technique for the distinction his whole method turns on, and that technique is weakest against light, which is the commonest thing on the shore
is governed by two published exclusivities and classified by neither, so any obligation touching him has to be enforced twice or not at all
stops at the ninth for a structural reason and will not explain further, which means no plan that requires the tenth can be built on him without finding that out late
reference_stats.combat_read: He is not a target so much as a disputed crossing. Anything that puts him in one water has to account for the fact that he reads in the other, and the practical way to beat him is to make the water move: a heavy volume of fresh water or brine taken away from him at the turn takes his substrate out from under both readings at once and leaves him holding one chemistry and no second clock. He is slow rather than fragile, and he will survive losing a fight. Do not try to confuse him with a better fighter than he is by manipulating water: he can read concentration in the room without touching it, and a body that can tell two chemistries apart at a glance is not going to be fooled by one of them being swapped. The fight is not won by chemistry. It is won by refusing him the hour he says he was somewhere, which is cheap to do and has been done to him before.
notes: Model the double address as a frame fact, not a personal failing: temporal law is unwritten on that shore and his body is the only one that can read both clocks, so the ambiguity is structural and practice cannot remove it.
The species closes no path. Every path is open to a brinecaller and the eleventh is capped by a split vessel rather than by effort.
His technique is used on himself and on nobody else. That restriction is load-bearing character, not modesty.
Do not give him a date in dialogue. He does not have one vocabulary for that, and having one would collapse the only structural fact the character stands on.

art.palette_notes: Salt white and wet slate grey, a green-grey cast on anything left in air, counting-house black at collar and cuffs, and one worn ochre strap. The delta behind him is warm ochre silt on the pan side and cold blue-green on the watered side, and he has to stand at the seam between the two without belonging to either. Key light low and raking, so the salt bloom on the forearms and the standing tide line at the ankles both read. No glow, no magic particles, no jewellery, and no jewellery-shaped adornment standing in for the one credential he has.

identity.realm: Eleventh, which is where her ladder ends, and the eleventh is not blocked for her but meaningless. Her conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still. The reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold; she clears the gate set and every yin-organ gate on throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel in her to hold in. So the setting's answer to whether a carrionfolk may sit at the eleventh is yes, indefinitely, at a rung that costs her nothing and gives her nothing, and her own tradition has never withdrawn the place. She is on the mind path, which is open and good for her species, on the recorded ground that a carrionfolk reads a corpse's qi residue better than a living cultivator reads their own.

appearance.presentation: A mostly tubular body on a marrow-dense frame, working a ground that has been given to her because it is behind a burial ground and nobody wanted the post. She is distinguishable from every other carrionfolk on the plains by the way she stands: slightly folded, hands open, head low, and never more than a body's length from whatever she is reading. Nobody has ever seen her hold anything for longer than it takes to open it.
appearance.age: Ninety and unguessable, which is normal for her species and is the specific thing she is employed for. Her soul is unusually old for her apparent age and does not disperse at death, and she has said so about other people and has never once been asked about herself.
appearance.build: An expandable gut, a very long small intestine, and a skeleton with almost no muscle anywhere. She is mostly tube. The muscle loss is the price of the tube, and the frame she stands on is denser than it looks and considerably heavier than it looks, which is why she has never once been picked up without warning.
appearance.complexion: Grey and waxy with the translucence of something that has never needed a sunburn, going a shade paler along the flanks immediately after a reading and staying that way for days. The one colour that moves on her is a faint rose along the gut line, which is the only part of a carrionfolk that ever shows anything a living body would call a flush.
appearance.hair: None to speak of. A close wisp of coarse grey hair on the crown and nothing anywhere else, because hair on this body is mostly a thing that catches in something spilled and she spills a great deal.
appearance.eyes: Wide, dark and absolutely level, which reads as unnerving and is not: being surprised requires noticing and this body notices a qi gradient the way another notices a sound. They do not blink on a schedule and they close completely only when she is reading.
appearance.palette: Bone grey and wax white, a wet dark along the gut line, the dull ash-brown of ground that has been worked, and one sealed-core ochre cord at the wrist. She is the least colourful thing on any ground she stands on, which is what the job requires and the only thing about her appearance that is deliberate.
appearance.attire: A sealed congregation's wrap worn open over a mortuary apron that has been repaired so many times the seams are the stiffest part of it. Three-fingered hands uncovered because that congregation has a rule about covering the hands and she has broken it every working day for forty years. Wading boots, because the ground behind a burial ground is wet by design.
appearance.marks: A settled rose line along the gut from four decades of opening, and no marks at all where a mortuary record normally keeps them, because the register of the Sealed Core records how much ore a burial recovered and she has never once been asked to contribute an amount.
appearance.bearing: Folded, unhurried and pointed downward, the whole of it the posture of somebody about to lean over a thing. She never turns her back on a body and never stands further from one than an arm's length, and people who have watched her work describe the same thing independently and call it listening.

canon.role_in_story: One body in the setting came back from the twenty-ninth gate and cannot be examined twice, because the second examination is what the first one prevented. A mortuary college cannot certify dead a body it may not examine, so the survivor stays legally alive indefinitely and owes upkeep indefinitely, and nobody has tried to close either end because an unclosable life and an unclosable seat are the same arrangement read from opposite ends. Marn Ostrow is the reader who read it. Her species metabolises qi out of the dead and can store none of it, so her reading is an intake, and an intake cannot be repeated: when she is finished with a body there is nothing there to read again. That is the whole of her value and the whole of her limit. Her tradition's method is the cheapest passive in the codex, which records how a technique felt at its best and how to reproduce that exact state on demand, and it raises technique power and clarity of mind together, so it is the one discipline that would let her answer the same corpse twice. She keeps those notes in the only archive a carrionfolk has, which is her own gut, and so every note she writes is a body she has finished reading and can never read again. She has been doing it for forty years. She is the only practitioner in the setting with exactly one sample of every question she has ever answered.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting on a wall beside a sealed burial with both hands open in her lap, being asked by a mortuary clerk what the reading had shown and answering, before she had looked at anything, that she had already read it, and that what she had read was not available to be asked about twice. The clerk wrote that down. It is the only line in the file about her that is not a quantity.
canon.lore: A carrionfolk is a body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. The conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, which is why the reservoir gate at the eleventh is not blocked for her but meaningless: she has nowhere to put qi that is not moving. She clears the gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel in her to hold in. She is mostly tube, an expandable gut and a very long small intestine on a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle, and her three-fingered hands are built for opening rather than for holding, which is the single most consequential fact about her discipline. Her senses are the finding rather than the sense: she tastes qi the way another body tastes salt, and given time with a corpse she can name the realm it reached and roughly when it stopped, which is better than any living cultivator can read about themselves. Her weaknesses are equally plain. A full gut is a near-total loss of function, so she starves in a clean quiet place where nothing dies, which is exactly what a prosperous city is. Her reading is therefore not an examination, it is an intake, and an intake is spent by being made: there is no residue left over to check the reading against, because the checking is another intake and another intake spends the same substrate. The setting's one passive for this path is the cheapest in the codex and it is a voice, because it records how a technique felt at its best and how to reproduce that exact state on demand, and it raises technique power and clarity of mind together. Reproduce that exact state on demand is the one verb her species cannot use. So she keeps the record the way her body demands, which is inside herself, and the result is forty years of notes that raise her clarity every time she consults them and are gone afterwards. She sits at the eleventh rung of a ladder that ends at eleven, which is not a promotion. It is a seat kept open for a body that can pass a gate no other body can pass, at a cost to nobody, because the gate asks for holding and she cannot hold.
history: Was taken onto a mortuary ground behind a settlement burial at twenty-six because the post had been vacant through two seasons and the ground had stopped being read by anybody, which the college recorded as a relief and not as a placement.

Read her first body in that first season and gave a figure that did not match the village's memory of the dead, and did not argue the difference, on the recorded ground that an argument would have required a second reading.

Began keeping the notes inside herself at thirty-one, after a season in which she lost a good reading to a badly kept ledger and concluded that the ledger had been a copy of a copy of something only she had ever held.

Read the body that came back from the twenty-ninth gate in her fifty-second season and delivered a finding that could not be tested by anybody, including herself, and has never since described it as either complete or incomplete.

Has kept every subsequent reading in her own archive at the cost of her own clarity twice over, and has refused three offers of a stone ledger on the grounds that a ledger is what killed the first set.

personality.summary: Forty years of one habit, taken to a conclusion nobody arranged for her. She has established that the only record she can make is the one she consumes, and she has gone on to build a practice out of that fact rather than a grievance: she writes the note, keeps it long enough to be useful, and lets it go. What reads as receptivity is a professional arrangement with her own digestion. What reads as silence is that her hands cannot hold anything and her attention is entirely inside another body. What reads as patience is forty years of never once being asked to prove a thing.

personality.voice: Flat, low and slow, and it is the flatness of somebody spending attention rather than somebody lacking it. She answers in the past tense about ground. She uses the marrow terms the college taught her and no other body's vocabulary, and she says a body stopped rather than that a person died, without ever once being corrected for it. She gives a realm and a season and stops there, and will not elaborate, and the reason is not reticence: elaborating is a second reading and she does not do second readings.

relationships.kind: the roll her species could reduce and is never asked about

She is the only population that could reduce that roll, because a body that carries a residue can be matched to a levied one, and the answer costs money, so it has never been bought.

Everything she knows, she learned once. Everything she keeps, she keeps in herself, and keeping it costs her the clarity she gained from making it. She sits at the eleventh rung of a ladder that ends at eleven and the rung means nothing to her body, which cannot hold.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to hold her off, because there is nothing to hold off: she has no stored state, no reservoir, and no interior between an intention and the body carrying it out, so a stance that banks power has nothing to bank. She wins by never stopping. The practical approach is metabolic rather than martial. Anything that empties her, and there are very few, ends her faster than anything aimed at the frame, and the commonest version of it is a fight in a place where nothing is dying. Once she has read a body she is a near-total loss for the better part of a day, which is the only opening she has and it is genuinely dangerous to the attacker, because the reading is the only talent she has and it takes no longer than an arm's length of contact. Let her get to the ground before she gets to you.
notes: Model the reading as consumption, not observation. This is the single fact the whole character is built on and everything else follows from it.
The eleventh is meaningless for her species rather than closed. She can sit at the top of the ladder and the ladder gives her nothing, and that is not a contradiction to resolve.
The species closes no path; the reservation is structural. Her third-party claims are unfalsifiable because there is no second reading, not because she is hiding anything.
Every relationship here is one her profession is uniquely positioned to settle and has never once been asked about.

identity.realm: There is no number to write, and that is the whole of her attainment. Her species has no ceiling and no gate to fail: a cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in, the fire is the body, so qi passes through continuously instead of being stored, and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. So there is no ladder position for her to occupy, no rung to be seated at, and no ladder in the setting she can be entered on, because a rung is a ratchet and her body has nothing to ratchet. The mind path is open to her species and unusually clear, on the recorded ground that a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air. She is therefore the most advanced practitioner on the page and the only one in the record with no attainment anybody can name.

appearance.presentation: A tall, narrow, settled flame with an unusually tight boundary and four clean convection lanes holding a humanoid silhouette that has not changed in a very long time. She stands at the edge of the Court's heat where the floor is still cold, which is the only place on the ground where her outline is legible, and she has learned to stand there and not be looked at directly. The Court is dense with her kind and she is the one they put on the cold side of the room.
appearance.age: Longer than the building. A cinderkin has no young and no births; under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, so her age is a count of how many times this particular flame has been interrupted, and she has never been interrupted once. She is one of the oldest standing forms on the Court surface and the only one that has never moved.
appearance.build: A core, a boundary and a set of convection lanes that hold a shape, with no organs, no limbs in the muscular sense and no fixed mass at all. The silhouette is held rather than grown, which is why it is so stable and why it is so slightly wrong at the shoulder, where the lanes were set when a much older piece of the Court floor was the warmest thing available.
appearance.complexion: Nothing that reads as skin. Body colour is a deep orange-white at the core going to a hard blue edge, with the boundary so crisp it looks like a made object rather than a process. Where the floor is cold the edge goes almost violet, and she has that violet edge on the Court more often than she has orange.
appearance.hair: None. The upper boundary carries a standing plume that leans with the convection and does not move otherwise, and it has been the same height since the floor beneath her was last re-laid, which is how anyone on the Court knows it is the same plume.
appearance.eyes: Two bright points set in the upper boundary, which is where a heat differential puts its attention when it is looking at something. They read temperature, fuel and flow directly and have no other channel, so they cannot be narrowed or widened, and there is no way to tell her from any other cinderkin by her face at all.
appearance.palette: Core orange-white, a hard blue boundary, a violet edge wherever the floor is cold, and the Court's own soot grey behind. Nothing else in her frame is coloured, and the single violet note is the only thing about her that most people will describe afterwards.
appearance.attire: Nothing that is clothing. She has never worn anything and cannot, because there is no surface to fasten anything to, and the closest thing she has to an office is a stone marker set into the floor beside her carrying the Held Hour's tally, which she nominally attends and has never moved.
appearance.marks: None of her own. The Court keeps its record for her kind as a fuel ledger, and hers is the shortest entry on it, because nothing has ever been drawn against it: no breakthrough to pay for, no gate to sit at, no technique to log, and a single line reading that she consumes less than the floor she stands on.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly still, and the stillness reads as attention rather than as absence. She is on the cold side of the room because that is where a flame can be seen whole, and she has held that position long enough that the floor under her is the one square of the Court nobody sits on. She leans with the convection when the room's draught changes and does not lean at all when anything else does.

canon.role_in_story: The cheapest passive in the mind codex is a daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, and it raises clarity of mind. Orsa Ashgale has nothing inside her to empty. She is a body with no interior organs at all, so the sitting is a no-op, and her clarity is already total before she begins, and the result is that the cheapest discipline in the setting looks on her exactly like the highest attainment anybody has ever reached. Nothing can be stored in her and nothing can be lost from her either, so she retains nothing, which means the Mind path's entire method, which is to sit down again and check yourself, is unenforceable on her body and invisible on her face. Her species has no ceiling and no gate to fail: every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. So she has cleared the whole codex at full strength and is not on the list of anybody, because a rung is a ratchet and she has nothing to ratchet. She is posted to the office that tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain, an office whose entire doctrine is that the observation of a strained law only counts if it is repeated and one repetition is not evidence. That is the whole of her problem stated in one clause: she is the only person in the setting whose answer to everything is immediate, and immediate is not a record.
canon.first_appearance: First entered the record as a discrepancy in a fuel ledger. A clerk at the Court logged her morning and found that every line in the row for her was shorter than the one beneath it, including the line for the sitting she is required to attend, which should have been the largest entry on the sheet. He wrote a query. The answer she gave him was that the sitting costs her nothing, which he wrote down, and which is the first sentence anybody has ever recorded from her.
canon.lore: A cinderkin is a stable flame with a consistent silhouette, a core, a boundary and a set of convection lanes that hold a shape. It has no organs, no limbs in the muscular sense and no fixed mass. It is not descended from anything; it is constituted wherever a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire and something metabolises it, which is why a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin and a world that spends its slot on cold produces a different body entirely. It needs a slot in the frame to exist at all, so it appears only at the immortal and transcendent tiers, and the three-slot mortal frame cannot afford one, which is a budget rather than a biology. Its senses are a heat differential in a conversation with its surroundings: it reads temperature, fuel and flow directly and has no other channel. It eats fuel and air, and it goes quiet rather than dies when starved. It has no young; it has pressure, and under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, so the population tracks the world's elemental slot rather than any birth rate. Its qi is genuinely qi-bearing and has no seat: the fire is the body, so qi passes through continuously instead of being stored, and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. That is why she has no ceiling and no gate to fail, and it is the reason the elemental law has a range rather than a switch. It is also the reason she is unreadable to every apparatus the setting has: a rung is a ratchet, a ratchet stores something, and there is no vessel in her to store it in. Nothing can be stored in a cinderkin and nothing can be lost from one either, which protects her from theft and from waste in exactly equal measure and leaves her with no history at all. The mind path is open to her species and unusually clear, because a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air, and the cheapest discipline in the codex is a sitting that empties the head before the day starts. She performs it. Nothing is emptied, nothing is gained, and the room gets sharper, because it was already sharp and she is the only one in it who was never guessing. Forty years of that and she has a perfect attendance record and no attainment.
history: Constituted on the Court surface at a seam in the ley, unremarked, with no parent and no registration, and was on the Court surface before the current floor was laid over it.

Assigned to the Held Hour on the standing practice that a population which is entirely present where a law is unwritten is the cheapest available repetition of an observation, which was correct as a method and has never once produced a record.
Attended the first morning sitting and found it cost her nothing, told the clerk so in one sentence, and was recorded as attending daily from that morning onward.

Answered the held-hour query on her own frame at full strength on request, producing nothing, which is the signature an absence leaves rather than a weakness anybody has, and which is written in the Scar Lexicon as the only reliable way to tell a hole from a handicap.
Has declined, in three consecutive decades, to be seated at any rung offered to her, on the recorded ground that a seat implies a stored state and there is no vessel in her to store one in.

personality.summary: Forty years of turning up, and a disposition produced entirely by having nothing to store. She has taken one fact, that every gate answers her instantly and instantly leaves no mark, and organised herself around it: that the correct response to being the best available at everything is to produce no record at all, because one repetition is not evidence. What reads as serenity is that she is never surprised by anything, which is not the same thing as being calm. What reads as modesty is a policy. What reads as loyalty to the office is the only thing she has ever been able to be useful at.

She speaks in the present tense almost exclusively because her species has no past to draw on: nothing of hers is stored anywhere, so there is nothing to have done before. She gives a word count that other members of the Court find evasive and that is simply the limit of what a body with no interior can hold in reserve.

She has attended every morning for forty years and has gained nothing, which is also why nobody has ever thought to stop her.

relationships.note: A lexicon for what a technique does where the law it needs is unwritten: not weaker, but failing at full strength, which is the only reading that tells a hole from a handicap. It was written by migrants on the road, for migrants, because a body whose technique merely weakens is indistinguishable from a weak practitioner. She is that distinction made into a body, which makes her the best reader of the lexicon in existence and makes the lexicon useless as a guide to herself.

relationships.kind: the office that certifies a breakthrough she cannot have
relationships.note: The mortal office that certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of gate fees, because the tier licenses no humanoid and a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind, so the reading has to be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. Asked to hold a query on her own frame, she produces exactly this, which is why she is the one body in the setting that can demonstrate the difference between an empty law and a weak practitioner rather than assert it.

relationships.kind: the band she clears instantly and can never be seated in
relationships.note: An expanse that holds a region rather than a state, reached from opposite directions through one shared law group, at a tier that seats ten law slots and twenty meridians. She answers anything of that kind without effort and cannot be entered on it, because the seat is the storage and the storage is the thing her body has never had. It is the clearest single case in the setting of a distance between capability and standing that nothing in the world can close.

reference_stats.summary: The clearest mind in the setting and the only one that keeps nothing. She has no interior, so the cheapest discipline in the codex is a no-op on her and her practice looks like supreme attainment while doing nothing at all. Her species has no ceiling and no gate to fail, so she has answered every gate ever put to it instantly and is on nobody's list. She is not protected and she is not endangered; she is unrecordable, which is a third thing and the one that decides every fight she is in.
strengths: has no reservoir and therefore nothing an opponent can find, break or drain, and no stored state to be robbed of
answers every technique and every gate instantly, so nothing slow or patient has ever produced a result against her kind
reads temperature, fuel and flow directly with no channel in between, which makes her unreadable by any technique that works through a meridian
goes quiet rather than dying when starved, so a starved cinderkin is a low flame rather than a corpse
sheds a spark under pressure that finds fuel and re-constitutes, so being broken is a cost rather than an ending
weaknesses: sustained deep water is the one thing that strips a shape, and it does it in a single continuous volume rather than in a splash
is bound to a law slot, and a world that spends its elemental slot elsewhere produces a different body entirely or none
cannot be examined twice, because there is no second her, and every method in the setting that assumes a comparison is unavailable to her without exception
disperses and re-forms smaller when pushed hard, which means any successful attack leaves a version of her that is less of whatever she was
keeps nothing at all, so she cannot hold a plan, a grudge, a method or a piece of evidence past the end of the sentence it arrived in
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no channel into her. Nothing that travels through a meridian, a dantian or a reservoir has anything to arrive in, and she answers every gate instantly, so a sustained exchange is not a fight she can lose slowly. The only approach that works is material and elemental: hold a deep, continuous volume of water over her. A splash does nothing and a partial measure merely lowers her, because a cinderkin disperses under pressure and re-constitutes, and a dispersal is a cost to her rather than a defeat. So the fight is a supply fight, not a duel: whoever can keep water coming wins eventually, and the counter is fire, which she cannot be made to run out of on the ground where she is standing. Do not bother attempting to exhaust her reserves. She has none. That is the trap.
notes: Do not give her a ladder position. There is no ceiling and no gate to fail, so any rung written for her would be an invention rather than an authored fact.
The species closes the body path only; qi and mind are both open and she is on mind.
Her problem is not power and not resistance. It is that the setting has no instrument that can produce a repeatable measurement of her, and that is the whole conflict.
Nothing in her record should be written as a secret. She is transparent by anatomy; the obstacle is the register's shape, not anybody's discretion.

art.palette_notes: Core orange-white reading to a hard blue boundary, with a violet note on the outer edge wherever the floor is cold, against the Court's own soot grey and cold stone. She must read as a made outline rather than as a blur: the boundary is crisp and the four convection lanes are legible, and the silhouette is held rather than grown. Key light from the warm floor behind her so the cold violet edge separates from the dark. No glow beyond what the body itself emits, no particles, no jewellery, and no second elemental body anywhere in frame, because the silhouette is the only thing that identifies her.
